summary: Autopilot imaging stalls when NIC ordering flips on dual Intel/Mellanox NIC systems
description:
Issue summary: Several staging workstations with dual NICs (integrated Intel + discrete Mellanox) intermittently hang during Autopilot/OOBE provisioning. The imaging job reaches the 'Applying network profile' step and then stalls with a DHCP timeout. Impact: Blocks a batch of 12 devices in staging, delaying a Dedicated capacity validation run scheduled for this week. Environment: Staging cluster, us-east region, Autopilot image v2026.02.04, driver-bundle v3.1.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Depot: replace NIC on Precision 7480 with a Mellanox ethernet card (HW swap).
2) Start Autopilot provisioning in staging with standard imaging task sequence.
3) Observe provisioning pause at network configuration / DHCP stage; device does not obtain lease and logs show conflicting MAC/persistent naming between eno and enp devices.

Observed behavior and logs:
- systemd-networkd reports: "link state change: new name enp4s0f1 -> eno1" followed by DHCPDISCOVER retransmits and eventual timeout.
- ip link output after stall sometimes shows duplicate MAC reported on ena and enp interfaces before networkd renames.
- Imaging scripts assume stable predictable interface name and apply DHCP client-id based on BIOS-derived MAC, leading to DHCP server treating the request as a different client and rate-limiting in our staging DHCP pool.

Business impact: Prevents successful provisioning of mixed-NIC SKUs in staging; could occur in Dedicated fleets after depot repairs. Blocking the planned Dedicated capacity soak test.

Attachments: staging logs (attached in ticket), WinPE trace from failed imaging run, sample output of 'ip link' and 'journalctl -u systemd-networkd' from affected device.
comments: Support (2026-02-10): Logged by depot technician after encountering 4/12 failures in today's batch. Provided initial logs and device serial numbers.
Miguel Torres (2026-02-10): Assigned for triage. Initial hypothesis: NIC driver/firmware causing MAC reenumeration and systemd renaming race during early boot. Will reproduce with lab unit.

Tech (2026-02-11): Reproduced on Lenovo P1 with Mellanox 10Gb card. Captured DHCP packet traces showing client-id mismatch after interface rename. DHCP server treats requests as new client and hits per-mac rate-limit we have in staging (isc-dhcp configured).

Miguel Torres (2026-02-11): Created ephemeral test image that disables predictable network naming in udev and forces bios-based naming as a stop-gap. Provisioning succeeds in test. Planning follow-up: update imaging-scripts to normalize interface names during WinPE stage and submit driver bundle update for Mellanox/Intel ordering compatibility.
investigation: Reproduced on hardware in lab: Dell Precision 7480 with onboard Intel i225 + Mellanox ConnectX-5 PCIe card.

Observed systemd-networkd renaming event: kernel enumerates Mellanox first in some boots causing interface indices to flip between boots; udev persistent net rules not present in current Autopilot image (we rely on predictable names but BIOS/ACPI changes up ordering).

Captured tcpdump during WinPE: DHCPDISCOVER sent with client-id derived from previous interface name resulting in new MAC being used; isc-dhcpd logs show 'rate limit exceeded for MAC' for the later requests.

Tested workaround: In WinPE pre-provision hook, we add 'ip link set dev * down; ip link set dev <primary> address <bios-mac>' then restart networkd; this produced successful DHCP lease in 10/10 runs in lab.
Checked driver bundles: Mellanox driver v5.6 present; vendor notes mention that firmware v1.11 may change link reporting order after cold reboots. Two devices had firmware v1.11, others v1.09.
Correlated with depot repair log: devices that had NIC replaced without firmware alignment showed higher failure rate.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: imaging-scripts PR #812 (linked) adds a WinPE pre-network hook that normalizes interface names and applies BIOS-derived MAC to presumed primary interface before requesting DHCP. Techs instructed to apply the temporary WinPE image for today's queues (manual staging).

Planned permanent fix: 1) Update Autopilot base image to include udev rules that generate stable interface aliases based on PCI slot and BIOS serial (RFC in Confluence). 2) Roll out driver-bundle v3.2 which pins Mellanox firmware to v1.09 where practical or applies vendor-recommended firmware consistency script in depot. 3) Add DHCP server exemption for provisioning pool to avoid per-MAC rate-limits during imaging where client-ids may shift.

Rollout notes: PR 812 is merged to the imaging-scripts feature branch; coordinate with Solutions Engineering to validate in staging on 2026-02-13. Depot team to hold off on broader deployment until driver-bundle v3.2 is tested. Follow-up tasks created: INT-214380 (driver bundle rollout), INT-214381 (udev rule merge + image bake).
next_steps: Deploy temporary WinPE image with PR #812 to staging cluster (owner: Depot Tech lead)
Schedule driver-bundle v3.2 test batch in staging (owner: Platform Reliability)
Prepare udev rule RFC and Confluence update for developer review (owner: Miguel Torres)
Adjust DHCP provisioning pool rate-limits for imaging windows (owner: Network Ops)
Create postmortem/retro if issue occurs during next dedicated soak test (owner: Support Lead)
